subject: GCP Marketplace: deferred accrual & dunning schedule for Horizon Labs
messages:
From: Accounting (Horizon Labs) <accounting@horizon-labs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected deferred accrual on GCP Marketplace invoice

Hi Ben,

We received our August GCP Marketplace invoice today and noticed a ~USD 38,400 line labelled ‘deferred accrual adjustment’ we don’t recognize. Our internal billing team did not change any subscription settings, and this pushed the invoice past our payment threshold which may trigger a dunning notice next week.

I’ve attached a short extract from our billing export (usage_snapshot_aug.csv) showing the invoice lines and the billing IDs. Can you help explain what triggered this deferred accrual and, if it’s on your side, provide a timeline for correction? Horizon Labs would like any dunning halted while we resolve.

Thanks,
Maya Rodriguez
Accounting Manager
Horizon Labs
attachments: usage_snapshot_aug.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Accounting (Horizon Labs) <accounting@horizon-labs.com>

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected deferred accrual on GCP Marketplace invoice

Hi Maya — thanks for the heads up and for sending the snippet. I’m copying Marissa (billing ops) and Jonas (marketplace ops) to triage.

Short answer: we saw a similar pattern for a small set of sellers last settlement cycle where GCP’s reconciliation window backfilled usage that had previously been in a pending state. We need to reconcile your invoice lines against our settlement feed and confirm whether the adjustment is a market-side accrual (GCP) or a Redwood-side accounting mapping.

Next steps:
- Marissa: can you pull Horizon’s internal invoice mapping and see if the billing IDs match the GCP settlement file?
- Jonas: please check if this is tied to the 7-day deferred accrual rule we flagged last quarter and whether a settlement override is available.
- Maya: we’ll aim to have an initial assessment by EOD Monday; if needed we’ll request a dunning hold with your collections contact while we verify.

Ben
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Accounting (Horizon Labs) <accounting@horizon-labs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Unexpected deferred accrual on GCP Marketplace invoice — initial reconciliation notes

Hi Maya / Ben,

I pulled Horizon’s invoice lines into our reconciliation tool and compared them to the GCP settlement file for the period 2026-08-01 → 2026-08-15. Preliminary findings:

- Line 1 (billing id: GCP-4721): originally invoiced as usage on 2026-08-05, but GCP marked ~USD 31,200 as ‘deferred’ and pushed it into a subsequent settlement batch on 2026-08-14.
- Line 2 (billing id: GCP-4789): small charge (~USD 7,200) that was flagged by GCP due to a SKU-migration reclassification.

Root cause candidate: a delayed event in GCP’s marketplace ingestion where a subset of usage records were ingested after the initial invoice cutoff — in our system that appears as a deferred accrual adjustment. This is consistent with the 7-day ingestion window we documented previously.

Action items I’m attaching: recon notes and a patch CSV that maps the GCP billing ids to your Horizon invoice ids (horizon_gcp_recon_notes.pdf; usage_correction_patch.csv).

Proposed remediation plan:
1) Redwood issues a short-form credit for the deferred accrual lines to prevent immediate payment pressure on Horizon.
2) We request a settlement correction with GCP Marketplace to ensure the amounts are re-attributed to the correct billing period (we’ll open HS-48922).
3) Put a temporary dunning hold on your account until the settlement correction completes (we’ll coordinate with your collections contact).

Target timeline: initial credit + dunning hold request by Tue 2026-08-24; settlement correction submitted to GCP the same day.

Let me know if you want a call — happy to jump on a 20-minute screen-share with the export.

– Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: horizon_gcp_recon_notes.pdf, usage_correction_patch.csv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Accounting (Horizon Labs) <accounting@horizon-labs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Unexpected deferred accrual on GCP Marketplace invoice — agreed next steps

Thanks all — quick summary and confirmation of next steps so Horizon has a single place to reference.

1) Redwood will issue a contra-invoice (credit memo) for USD 38,400 covering the deferred accrual lines as an interim measure. That will appear on your Redwood billing statement; we’ll follow with a corrected settlement once GCP completes the re-attribution.
2) We have submitted HS-48922 with GCP Marketplace Support to request reclassification of the late-ingested usage; GCP acknowledged and provided an incident id. We will push for priority handling and share updates in the HubSpot ticket.
3) Dunning hold: Redwood Collections will place a temporary hold on any dunning actions for Horizon through 2026-09-05. If GCP completes settlement correction earlier we will release the hold and issue the corrected invoice/credit reconciliation.
4) Owner and points-of-contact:
   - Redwood billing ops: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com) — will own the credit memo and reconciliation.
   - Redwood marketplace ops: Jonas Weber (jonas.weber@redwood.com) — will manage the GCP engagement (HS-48922).
   - Horizon collections: Maya Rodriguez (accounting@horizon-labs.com).

Related artifacts: HubSpot record HS-48922 (https://hubspot.redwood.com/record/HS-48922) and reconciliation folder (https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/0B_recon_horizon_august).

If that aligns with Horizon’s expectations, we’ll proceed and confirm when the credit memo posts (ETA 48 hours).

Best,
